blocks.text: Watch a video about machine provisioning keys (shows legacy UI).

The provisioning key is a text string that is generated when you add a machine provisioning key in the Zscaler Admin Console. You need to add the key to a Zscaler Client Connector profile rule for Windows or macOS. When added, the provisioning key functions like an ID to the machine, and it enables the Private Access cloud to verify the machine's authenticity prior to logging into Windows or macOS.

Provisioning keys should be treated as secrets and properly protected because they can create a resource for a tenant. The provisioning key must also be secured and not transmitted or stored in clear text.
Machine provisioning keys provide the following benefits and allow you to:

blocks.item: Associate the Zscaler Client Connector with a machine group.
Enable Machine Tunnels for Pre-Windows Login to gain access to internal applications even when the device's Zscaler Client Connector is not connected to Zscaler Admin Console.

Before logging into Zscaler Client Connector, you must configure machine provisioning keys and machine groups in order to use a machine tunnel to establish a connection to a service. To learn more, see About Machine Tunnels.
Provisioning keys are considered confidential information and must be kept in a safe place. For each provisioning key, a Copy Provisioning Key option is provided to copy the key to your clipboard.

blocks.heading: About the Machine Provisioning Keys Page

blocks.text: On the Machine Keys page (Administration > Private Access Authentication > Machine Provisioning Keys), you can:

blocks.item: Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. To learn more, see Using Tables.
Refresh the Machine Provisioning Keys page to reflect the most current information.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
View a list of all the provisioning keys that are configured for your organization. For each provisioning key, you can see:

Name: The name of the key. This is the name you see when adding the key to a Zscaler Client Connector profile rule. To learn more, see Configuring Zscaler Client Connector App Profiles. You can also click the name of the provisioning key to open the Machine Provisioning Key Details drawer where you can view additional details about the provisioning key.
Machine Group: The machine groups that are using this provisioning key.
Status: Indicates whether the machine provisioning key is enabled or disabled.
Provisioning Key: The key needed to enable the cloud to verify the machine's authenticity prior to logging in to Windows.
This entry is blank if you disabled the View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation option when adding a machine provisioning key.
Copy the provisioning key to your clipboard. When deploying a machine, you are prompted to enter the key.

This icon is hidden for security purposes if you disabled the View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation option when adding a machine provisioning key. If the provisioning key doesn't appear, and a backup of the provisioning key isn't securely stored in an external credential vault, a new key must be generated. A new provisioning key can be created and attached to the same machine.
Download the provisioning key as a text file.
